purpose: Market-neutral rewrite of the HERO knowledge-check bank. Removes every reference to the UK, to the pilot, and to the Brand Captain role, so the same modules can be run unchanged in any market.
harvested_from: Deployed source in github.com/enerbartoli/mod1-knowledge-check @ main, fetched 2026-08-17. NOT from KC_Canonical_QuestionBank_v1_2026-08-06.json, which is stale for mod2 Q7, mod2 Q11 and mod4 Q4.
invariants: No correct answer letter moves. Prior submissions stay scoreable against the same key.
No question is added or removed. Module lengths and pass thresholds are unchanged.
No question states who captures at Level 2.5. Ownership at that level varies by market and is deliberately left unspecified.
No em-dash in any newly authored string.

options.A.new: Level 2.5 starts from the Daybreak baseline directly, and corrections for commercial or supply events are captured as Base Trend adjustments.

rationale.new: When the team has assessed that Daybreak's reduction is too aggressive, because there is not enough history for a structural reset, the correct path is to recalculate demand with commercial knowledge and lock the agreed view via an L2.5 Base Trend adjustment using the Level 2.5 reconciliation template.

questions.reason: Rewritten on 7 August 2026 to contrast the UK against the US. The teaching point is that the rule is per-market, so it can be taught with two unnamed markets and lands harder.

text.old: In the UK pilot, DI and FAN are not forecast statistically, so Daybreak produces no baseline for them. In the US, DI is forecast statistically. Where does the full forecast volume land in the Reconciliation Template in each case?
text.new: Two markets treat Direct Import (DI) differently. One has agreed not to forecast it statistically, so Daybreak produces no baseline for it. The other forecasts it statistically. Where does the full forecast volume land in the Reconciliation Template in each case?

options.A.old: UK DI and FAN: the full volume as Base Trend at Level 1. US DI: adjustments layered on the statistical baseline.
options.A.new: No baseline: the full volume as Base Trend at Level 1. With a baseline: adjustments layered on the statistical baseline.

options.B.old: Both: the full volume as Base Trend at Level 1, since DI and FAN always sit outside the statistical model.
options.B.new: Both: the full volume as Base Trend at Level 1, since DI always sits outside the statistical model wherever it is planned.

options.C.old: Both: adjustments layered on the resultant, since every segment carries a baseline once the cycle opens.
options.C.new: Both: adjustments layered on the resultant, since every segment carries a baseline once the cycle opens.

options.D.old: UK DI and FAN: the full volume as Base Trend at Level 2.5. US DI: the full volume as Base Trend at Level 1.
options.D.new: No baseline: the full volume as Base Trend at Level 2.5. With a baseline: the full volume as Base Trend at Level 1.

rationale.old: ... Where there is a baseline, as with DI in the US, the segment behaves like any other ...
rationale.new: What decides this is not the channel or the item class, it is whether the market agreed to forecast that segment statistically. Where there is no Daybreak baseline, the full volume enters as Base Trend at Level 1, and the Level 1 lock is essentially all Base Trend with no statistical signal to challenge against. Where there is a baseline, the segment behaves like any other: the resultant is the starting point and the team layers enrichments and Base Trend on top. The resultant itself is never overwritten in either case.

options.D.old: Evergreen is a United Kingdom-only exception that does not apply in North America or in Europe.
options.D.new: Evergreen is a single-market exception that does not apply anywhere else in the program.

rationale.old: Sales Operations owns the Evergreen designation. Not the Key Account Manager, not Demand Planning, not the Brand Captain. ...
rationale.new: Sales Operations owns the Evergreen designation. Not the Key Account Manager, not Demand Planning, not the brand team. Once an item is designated, it stops being built bottom-up and sits on a Daybreak baseline that the KAM enriches on top, like any Carry-Forward item. The designation is not automatic and it is not a market-specific quirk: what varies by market is which segments start outside the statistical model in the first place.

text.old: In what order do the four UK reconciliation sessions run, and who owns each?
text.new: In what order do the four reconciliation sessions run?

options.A.old: Marketing+DP -> Brand Captain -> KAM -> Market Leader.
options.A.new: Joint top-down challenge -> Level 2.5 Base Trend -> Level 1 commercial -> Sign-Off.

options.B.new: Level 1 commercial -> joint top-down challenge -> Level 2.5 Base Trend -> Sign-Off.

options.C.old: Brand Captain (Baseline) -> KAM (Commercial) -> Marketing + DP -> Market Leader (Sign-Off).
options.C.new: Level 2.5 Base Trend -> Level 1 commercial -> joint top-down challenge -> Sign-Off.

options.D.old: KAM -> Brand Captain -> Market Leader -> Marketing + DP.
options.D.new: Level 1 commercial -> Level 2.5 Base Trend -> Sign-Off -> joint top-down challenge.

rationale.old: The cascade is fixed: Captain at L2.5 first -> KAM at L1 -> Marketing+DP for the top-down challenge -> Market Leader for sign-off.
rationale.new: The cascade is fixed: Level 2.5 Base Trend first, then the Level 1 commercial session, then the joint top-down challenge, then Sign-Off. Each session opens only once the previous one has closed.

rationale.old: Strict sequencing - the handoff between sessions is a hard gate. If Captain has not finished at 2.5, Commercial does not start; if Commercial has not confirmed L1, Marketing+DP does not start; and so on.
rationale.new: Strict sequencing: the handoff between sessions is a hard gate. If Level 2.5 has not closed, the Level 1 commercial session does not start; if Level 1 is not confirmed, the joint top-down session does not start, and so on.

options.B.new: The three references are a temporary experiment that is intended to replace formal guardrail thresholds permanently, in every market.

Where they have not been defined yet, the team triangulates using AIM at BU/Brand, historical actuals at Brand x Forecasting Partner, and POS Glidepath at SKU. The three references stand in for guardrails, they do not replace them.
